transcript: Header: 2025-01-28 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~64 min | Location: videoconf | Recording: yes
[00:00:05] Nina: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro from Redwood side — I'm Nina, account exec, with Jason on the line, our SE. Claire might jump in a little later.
[00:00:22] Rajiv: Morning / afternoon all. I'm Rajiv, CTO at Evenflow Health — happy to be here, we want to move quickly on approvals.
[00:00:30] Derek: Derek here, procurement — main ask is clarity on billing cadence and thresholds that trigger a pricing committee.
[00:00:38] Marie: Marie, Head of Security. We'll be focusing on KMS, retention, and the DPA's handling of PHI. Also curious about access logs/audit trails.
[00:00:51] Sofia: Sofia from Legal — I'll be doing the MSA/DPA review and marking any healthcare-specific exceptions.

[00:01:05] Jason: Thanks — quick agenda: go through high-level commercial items, go over security/KMS, then technical options for deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private), and confirm next steps for procurement and benchmarks.

[00:01:20] Nina: Sound good. We do have an existing MSA template and a security exhibit; we can highlight the usual redlines customers ask for — data deletion windows, audit logs retention, and subprocessor disclosures.

[00:02:01] Rajiv: On deployment — our default preference is private deployment or VPC with customer-managed keys. We need to understand if Redwood supports HSM-backed KMS and key-holding vs bring-your-own-key.

[00:02:18] Jason: Yes — support both models. We offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in major clouds; HSM-backed KMS integration is supported, we can provide diagrams. Small caveat: some hosted plans have restrictions on full key custody, but Dedicated and Private routes allow customer key control.
[00:02:45] Marie: When you say 'restrictions', what exactly is limited? Do you retain any ability to decrypt under support scenarios? That's a big no for us with PHI.

[00:02:58] Jason: For hosted standard, there may be support workflows that use ephemeral keys for debugging, but we can commit to policies in the DPA and exhibit — for PHI workload we recommend Dedicated or Private where keys are strictly customer-controlled. We'll put that in writing.
[00:03:20] Sofia: We need contractual language that forbids access except under court order and with notice; also proof of key rotation and key destruction policies.
[00:03:33] Nina: Understood. We'll surface the security exhibit and propose redlines. One operational ask: audit log retention — how many months do you retain token-level call logs by default?

[00:03:48] Jason: Default is 90 days for the hosted logs; with Dedicated you can extend retention or export logs to your SIEM. With Private deploy, logs live in your environment and we don't ingest them.
[00:04:05] Marie: 90 is a bit short for audits — can we get an SLA for log exports? Prefer to push logs to our Splunk for 12 months.
[00:04:13] Jason: Yes — we can provide export hooks; the DPA can add a clause stating log export availability and SLAs for retention and export windows.
[00:04:30] Derek: On pricing — our procurement guidelines require an expected monthly burn range before we start long-term commitments. If we do a pilot, what's the typical credit or pilot pricing?

[00:04:44] Nina: For pilots we usually provide credits and a discounted pilot rate. We'll need to know expected throughput and token volumes. Also, we have Reserved/Dedicated proposals for commit pricing.
[00:04:58] Rajiv: We'll want to run a 48-hour benchmark of our core prompt patterns to check latency and cost per 1k tokens. Can you provision sandbox for that?
[00:05:10] Jason: Absolutely. We'll spin up a sandbox with sample model variants and allow 48h of runs. We'll also instrument for prefix caching and batching to show cost delta.
[00:05:28] Marie: Export controls — we operate in EU and US; any third-party subprocessors outside those regions? This impacts residency and signing authorities.
[00:05:40] Nina: We list subprocessors in the DPA appendix. We can confirm region-specific deployments; Redwood has EU-hosted regions and Private packages as well.
[00:05:55] Sofia: A question on indemnity caps and carve-outs for healthcare regulatory fines — any precedent in your MSA?

[00:06:04] Nina: The standard MSA has mutual indemnities with caps by contract value. We can surface recent exceptions and propose language that handles regulatory fines specifically; will flag for legal.
[00:06:20] Derek: Also need clarification on billing: net-30? billing contact? invoices to be sent to AP, but procurement needs the approval threshold number.
[00:06:31] Nina: Standard is net-30; we can support ACH and wire. We'll confirm billing contact detail and show the pricing tiers so you can map thresholds.
[00:06:48] Rajiv: Technical quibble — does Redwood support KV cache warmup if we warm the cache locally? We have predictable prompt prefixes for patient summaries.

[00:06:58] Jason: Yes — the runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching; it's sometimes called 'kayvee' in notes — sorry, that's a transcription habit — but yes we support that and we'll show cache hit rates in the benchmark.
[00:07:13] Marie: For the DPA, we need deletion window controls. Can Redwood guarantee deletions from backups and logs within X days?

[00:07:23] Jason: Deletion SLA depends on deployment. Hosted has a 90-day backup retention footprint, but we can discuss shorter windows on Dedicated and Private. We'll propose options in the exhibit.
[00:07:43] Sofia: We'll likely ask for purge-by-request clauses with proof of deletion. Also need to add clause for backup destruction timelines.
[00:07:53] Nina: We'll add those items to the redline set — and provide evidence of processes where possible.
[00:08:10] Derek: Who will be the Redwood signee and billing owner on the contract? Need legal contact for the MSA execution path.
[00:08:20] Nina: Redwood's commercial signee is usually our Head of Revenue; I'll identify the exact signer and include contact info in the follow-up.
[00:08:33] Rajiv: One more point on KMS key custody — we want BYOK with HSM and quarterly rotation. Can we put rotation orchestration into the runbook?

[00:08:45] Jason: Yes — we can document rotation, access control lists, and emergency key access procedures. For Private, rotation is fully customer-managed; for Dedicated we integrate with your KMS and rotate according to your schedule.
[00:09:05] Marie: Also need audit trail for any support engineering sessions that access logs or metadata. How do you surface those?
[00:09:14] Jason: Support sessions are logged; we can append a contract clause that any access requires a request ticket, justification, and will be recorded in audit logs with retention.
[00:09:34] Sofia: Regarding export controls, do you have a standard export control questionnaire we can use?
[00:09:39] Nina: Yes — we have a vendor questionnaire and an export control checklist; I'll attach those. It includes subprocessors, regions, and encryption standards.
[00:10:02] Derek: On the procurement timeline — we want to push this through within three weeks if possible. What are blockers from your side?
[00:10:12] Nina: Blockers typically are legal redlines or financial approvals. We'll aim to get the redlines to you within a week so your team can review before the Feb 6 pricing committee.
[00:10:25] Rajiv: Ok good. For the sandbox benchmark, will you provide sample metrics dashboard or raw logs so we can ingest to our observability?
[00:10:33] Jason: We'll provide both — raw logs for ingestion and a pre-built dashboard that shows latency percentiles, token cost, and cache hit rate.
[00:10:48] Nina: We'll also include a short FAQ noting differences between hosted/dedicated/private in page form.
[00:10:58] Marie: If we push for Dedicated, what's the SLA on latency and uptime? We need 99.9% with 200ms P95 for prompts under 512 tokens ideally.

[00:11:09] Jason: Our Dedicated plans can aim for 99.9% and low P95s; exact latency numbers depend on model and routing — for 512 tokens we often see P95 under 250ms in Dedicated, but we'll capture numbers in the benchmark.
[00:11:25] Sofia: On indemnity — any carveouts for willful misconduct?
[00:11:30] Nina: Standard carveouts apply. We'll surface the exact language and any options for negotiation.
[00:11:40] Derek: Could you also confirm data residency options for EU-only processing?
[00:11:45] Jason: Yes — EU region-only deployments are supported; Private gives the strongest guarantee, but we can commit to EU-only processing in the DPA for Hosted with region pinning.
[00:11:59] Rajiv: Great. Let's talk timeline: Nina you'll send redlines; Jason will prep KMS docs and sandbox; procurement schedules pricing committee — any objections?
[00:12:10] Sofia: No objections. We will review and come back with a consolidated redline doc.

[00:12:18] Nina: Recap then: Redwood sends MSA redline and security exhibit, KMS runbook and HSM notes, sandbox creds for 48h benchmark. Evenflow will schedule pricing committee and return DPA comments. Action owners noted in the deck.
[00:12:33] Derek: One last admin — can you provide PO templates or standard billing terms so AP can pre-authorize?
[00:12:40] Nina: Yes — will include PO template and invoice routing info.
[00:12:48] Rajiv: Thanks all. If no other items, we'll wrap. Appreciate the quick sync and we'll push internally to meet the dates.
[00:12:56] Nina: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts. Claire (SE) will pop in later if technical questions come up in the benchmark.
[00:13:05] End of recording
